Read a filled label sheet

Source: R/doc-labels.R
gr_read_labels.Rd

Reads one or more sheets written by gr_label_sheet(), checks every value and id, and returns the labels in the form the package's comparisons take: a screening reference for gr_calibrate(), a table for gr_extract_agreement(), calibration labels, or labels to compare a judge's verdicts with in hr_agreement(). A calibration sheet written with blind = FALSE gives a graded set hr_calibrate_signal() takes, with or without items: without them, the sheet's model_score column is read back as the number score. A blind one gives reference answers, and the model's answers must be scored against them to make the correct column it needs.

Usage

gr_read_labels(path, kind, items = NULL, fields = NULL)

Arguments

path

One or more CSV files written by gr_label_sheet() (one per reviewer), or the sheet as a data frame.

kind

The kind the sheet was written as.

items

The items the sheet was written from. Optional; with them, ids are checked against the items and the items' other columns (cluster, split, inclusion_prob, a signal's score and so on) are joined to the labels by item_id.

fields

For kind = "extraction": names, a gr_fields() schema or a gr_protocol(). A schema also checks each value's type. NULL takes every column of the sheet that is not an id, item, model or note column.

Value

A data frame with one row per sheet row: item_id, reviewer when there are several, the item columns, the decisions and the note, then any columns joined from items. An item column named like one of the sheet's decision or note columns (answer, verdict and so on, often the model's own output) is joined as model_<name>, unless the sheet already has a column of that name. answerable and correct are logical; human_decision and verdict are lower case; extraction values are text as written. A calibration result has a cluster column (from items, else document), and a correct column only when the sheet was written with blind = FALSE; only then is it ready for hr_calibrate_signal(). Its score comes from items when they are given, else from the sheet's model_score (yes and no, or TRUE and FALSE, read as 1 and 0; left out when a value is not a number). Attributes label_kind and unlabelled (the number of rows not yet labelled) are set.

What is checked

  • Every row has an item_id, and no id appears twice for one reviewer. With items, every id is one of the items', and an item missing from the sheets is reported with a warning of class gr_labels_missing.

  • Yes-or-no columns (answerable, correct) hold yes, no, y, n, true, false, 1 or 0, in any case. human_decision holds include or exclude, and verdict pass or fail.

  • An answerable QA or calibration item has an answer, and one that is not answerable has none; an item whose answerable is empty has no other decision filled; a calibration sheet with a correct column has it filled on every labelled row.

  • An extraction row with any field filled has every field filled (with "not reported" where the document does not report it), and with a schema each value reads as its field's type: a whole number, a number, yes or no, or one of an enum field's values.

Every value that fails is collected, and the error, of class gr_bad_labels, names the sheet, the row (counting the header as row 1, as a spreadsheet does) and the item. Its problems field holds them all. A row whose first decision column is empty is an item not yet labelled: it is returned with its decisions NA, and counted.

See also

gr_label_sheet(), gr_calibrate(), gr_extract_agreement(), hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_agreement()

Other reference sets: gr_label_sheet(), hr_assign_splits()

Examples

qa <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "a.pdf", "b.pdf"),
                 question = c("What was revenue?", "Who audited it?",
                              "When did the trial start?"))
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "qa-read.csv")
gr_label_sheet("qa", qa, path = path)
#> Wrote 3 item(s) to '/tmp/Rtmp4M7RcG/qa-read.csv', with instructions in '/tmp/Rtmp4M7RcG/qa-read_instructions.txt'. Read the filled sheet back with gr_read_labels().

# A person fills it in; here the filling is simulated.
sheet <- read.csv(path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
sheet$answerable <- c("yes", "no", "yes")
sheet$answer <- c("45.2 million dollars", NA, "March 2019")
write.csv(sheet, path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")

gr_read_labels(path, "qa", items = qa)
#> Read 3 row(s): 3 labelled, 0 not yet labelled.
#>   item_id document                  question answerable               answer
#> 1 qa-0001    a.pdf         What was revenue?       TRUE 45.2 million dollars
#> 2 qa-0002    a.pdf           Who audited it?      FALSE                 <NA>
#> 3 qa-0003    b.pdf When did the trial start?       TRUE           March 2019
#>   quote note
#> 1  <NA> <NA>
#> 2  <NA> <NA>
#> 3  <NA> <NA>
